description: We’re a team based in Casablanca, Morocco, taking on the "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars" challenge. We’re interested in astrophysics, space science, coding, and working with astronomical data. No NASA Space Apps experience needed, just curiosity, willingness to learn, and a desire to contribute!
summary:
My project consists of an interactive, walk-in virtual gallery where visitors can explore a collection of "artworks", each representing one or more spacecraft left behind on the Moon, Mars, and elsewhere in our solar system.

Each exhibit features information about the spacecraft, explaining what it is, why it was originally sent into space, the purpose and importance of its mission, and the scientific discoveries it made and continues to contribute to. It also explores an interesting question: why couldn't we bring these spacecraft back to Earth?

The project addresses the challenge by transforming space exploration history into an engaging and creative educational experience, helping school-age students and casual space enthusiasts discover and learn about the human-made hardware left beyond Earth and how these early missions paved the way for modern rovers and future exploration.
details:
My project is a virtual gallery with an intuitive interface where visitors can move around using the WASD keys, just like in video games. Each "artwork" represents a spacecraft left behind on the Moon, Mars, or elsewhere in our solar system. When clicked, it displays information about the spacecraft and its mission, which can also be read aloud.

The descriptions address some of the main questions: Why was the mission so important? What was the spacecraft originally sent into space to do? What scientific discoveries did it make, and what does it continue to teach us? And why couldn't we bring it back to Earth?

The intended impact is to make this information accessible to everyone, from school-aged children to adult space enthusiasts. I want to highlight that just because these spacecraft were left behind doesn't mean they have been forgotten. Their missions contributed to the scientific progress we've made and paved the way for many of the achievements that followed and those yet to come.

I developed the virtual gallery using XIBIT3600. Throughout the process, I wanted to make it fun and easy to use, while keeping it free, intuitive, and informative. I also paid attention to the descriptions, making sure they were concise, interesting, and easy to understand.

What makes this project creative is the combination of two things I hold close to my heart: museum culture and space. I wanted to turn the history of spacecraft and their missions into an interesting museum visit, giving these often-overlooked pieces of space history the attention they deserve.
